caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 119 of 1999 with CR 349 (FM) 1999
lawyer:
Md Mostafa, Advocate — For the Appellants. 
Gazi Sayedul Haque, Advocate — For the Respondents.
parties:
President, Magura Town Hall & another ------ Appellant
vs
President, Magura District Ainjibi Samity and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 4. The respondent as defendant resisted the aforesaid application for temporary injunction denying all its material allegations and contended, inter alia, that the plaintiff has no prima facie arguable case for injunction it has been contended that the CS Khatian stands in the name of Charu Chandra Sen as Secretary of Magura Town Hall and not as the Secretary of Magura Ainjibi Samity. It has also been asserted that Mr Charu Chandra Sen, although was a lawyer and a member of the plaintiff Samity, he was never the Secretary of the plaintiff Samity at any point of time and all assertion to the contrary are false and concocted. It has been further asserted that the finally published SA Khatian also stands in the name of Advocate Charu Chandra Sen as the Secretary of Magura Town Hall and not as the Secretary of Magura Bar Association as alleged by the plaintiff. It was stated that by a resolution passed in 1953 at the instance of the then SDO, Magura Theatre was renamed as Magura Town Hall and constitution was adopted for the Magura Town Club making provision for taking two members from the local Bar Association to the Executive Committee of the defendant Club as a matter of convenience but not as a matter of compulsion. It has been also asserted that by a regular resolution duly approved in the general meeting of the members of the defendant Samity the decision for reconstruction and development was taken and a construction Sub-Committee containing two members from the local Bar Association was formed in keeping with the previous practice. It has been stated that by registered Kabuliyat dated 23-1-18 the defendant took lease of the suit property in the name of Advocate Charu Chandra Sen clearly describing him as the Secretary of Magura Theatre subsequently renamed as Magura Town Club and not as the Secretary of Magura Ainjibi Samity. It has been alleged that Magura Town Hall is being run, managed and administered in accordance with its constitution, which was finally adopted in 1980 and nobody, including the plaintiff, ever took any exception to it at any point of time. It has been further alleged that in pursuance of the resolution dated 24-10-97, duly approved by the General Meeting of the defendant Club to the effect that a modern shopping complex be constructed in the suit premises a sub-committee was duly formed for supervision of the construction work and tender was invited from intending contractors, the lowest tender was ultimately accepted and work order was given in pursuance thereof. It has also been contended that the rent from the existing eight shops standing in the suit premises amounting to Taka 6,400.00 is being spent towards payment of salary to the clerk, peon, sweeper and towards payment of water rates, electricity charges and the like income and expenditure of the defendant Club are being properly maintained and audited. It has been further contended that the Magura Pourasava duly approved the plan submitted by the defendant and the on-going construction work is being carried on accordingly. It has been contended that more than Taka 1,10,001.00 has already been spent in the on-going construction work and the order of ad-interim injunction has already caused heavy losses and injury to the defendant Club and if an order of temporary injunction is passed against the defendant, the entire project will be destroyed causing irreparable loss and injury to the defendant. It was asserted that the balance of convenience and inconvenience stands heavily against the plaintiff and in favour of the contesting defendant.
